test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Indian sea ports is located in the far south as compared to the others?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Tuticorin.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Tuticorin seaport**

__
 
• Tuticorin seaport is located in the far south as compared to the others.
 
• Tuticorin Port is one of the 12 major ports in India.
 
• It is located in the state of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It was declared to be a major port on 11 July 1974.
 
• It is the second-largest port in Tamil Nadu and the fourth-largest container terminal in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Chennai port**

 
• Chennai Port, formerly known as Madras Port.
 
• It is the second largest container port of India, behind Mumbai's Nhava Sheva.
 
• The port is the largest one in the Bay of Bengal.
 
• It is the third-oldest port among the 13 major ports of India with official port operations beginning in 1881.

**Mangalore port**

 
• Mangalore Port is small water, all-weather port at Panambur, Mangalore in Karnataka state in India.
 
• It is the deepest inner harbor on the west coast.
 
• It is the only major port in Karnataka and the seventh largest port in India.

**Paradip port**

 
• Late Biju Patnaik, the then Chief Minister of Odisha, is the founder father of Paradip Port.
 
• It is the only Major Port in the State of Odisha situated 210 nautical miles south of Kolkata and 260 nautical miles north of Visakhapatnam on the east coast on the shore of Bay of Bengal.
